speaker: alse_pinder
text: The big book is off the shelf. The cat has been up the stair to see the cloth gone, and he is offended in a personal way.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I am carrying the loaf, which is still a finger short of the notch, so I shall ask. Are you beginning a play, or are you only troubling Master Field's property?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am reading. I am not beginning. Nobody in it has a line.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Then I have nothing to ask you to say again. When do you take the horse?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Wednesday, at first light, from the Bull. Tomorrow is the quarter. Tomorrow is not the road.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Tomorrow you put twenty shillings on my table before noon, and we see about the chamber. I am not letting it, and I am not settling it over a short loaf. Brooke stays where you left him.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Brooke stays. The chronicle goes back under the cloth before I sleep. The bay is still not taken.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I shall tell the cat the book is coming back. He will not believe a person who cannot read. He never does.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I let you the room, Master Shakespeare. I did not undertake that the weather should remain outside the stair.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The stair can keep its weather. Here is the threepence for the meal. Tomorrow is still the quarter, and not this loaf.
